facts.t: The River Boards Act, 1956 has never been used
facts.d: Parliament passed it the same year as the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act to create basin-level coordination bodies. Not a single river board has ever been effectively constituted under it — seventy years of a dead letter on the statute book.

facts.t: Article 262 can shut the Supreme Court out
facts.d: It permits Parliament to bar the jurisdiction of all courts, including the Supreme Court, over inter-state water disputes — and the 1956 Act does exactly that. In practice appeals still reach the Court through Article 136, which is why tribunal and Court roles overlap so messily.

The Mahanadi dispute between Chhattisgarh and Odisha has been before its tribunal since 2018, through periods when the same party governed both states and the Centre. Water disputes track river basins and regional identity, not party lines.

bank.q: With reference to the constitutional framework for water, consider the following statements:
s: Water supplies, irrigation and canals fall under Entry 17 of the State List.
Entry 56 of the Union List allows the Centre to regulate inter-state rivers if Parliament declares it expedient in the public interest.
Article 262 allows Parliament to bar the jurisdiction of courts over inter-state water disputes.
bank.e: All three are correct, and together they explain why water is simultaneously a state subject and a recurring federal flashpoint.

bank.q: Which tribunal is still under adjudication?
bank.e: The Mahanadi Tribunal, constituted in 2018 for the Chhattisgarh–Odisha dispute. Mahadayi decided in 2018 and Vansadhara in 2017.

bank.q: Match List I (tribunal) with List II (states principally involved):
bank.e: Mahadayi concerns Goa, Karnataka and Maharashtra; Vansadhara Andhra Pradesh and Odisha; Mahanadi Chhattisgarh and Odisha; Ravi and Beas Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT among the structural or legal issues in Indian water federalism?
o: Federal-jurisdictional ambiguity between Centre and States
Overlap between tribunal and Supreme Court roles
Outdated agreements arising from changed state boundaries
A single national water regulator with binding enforcement powers
bank.e: No such regulator exists. Its absence is part of the problem, not one of the problems in the list.

bank.as: Tribunal awards are frequently not complied with.
bank.rs: State governments face electoral pressure in the basin regions concerned.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. Water disputes become regional-identity issues, which is why depoliticising the discourse appears in every reform list.

bank.q: Which two Acts of 1956 form the statutory core of inter-state river governance?
o: The Water Act and the Environment Protection Act
The Inter-State River Water Disputes Act and the River Boards Act
The River Boards Act and the Water Act
The Inter-State River Water Disputes Act and the Interstate Council Order
bank.e: Both were passed in 1956. The disputes Act created the tribunal system; the River Boards Act was never effectively used.

bank.q: Consider the following global practices cited as models:
s: Integrated River Basin Management under the EU Water Framework Directive.
The Murray-Darling Basin Authority in Australia.
The United States Geological Survey as a credible, transparent data institution.
bank.e: All three are cited, alongside water markets in Australia and Chile as a scarcity-allocation mechanism.

bank.q: All of the following are technical or ecological issues in water governance EXCEPT:
o: A supply-augmentation bias favouring dams over demand management
Climate change breaking down historical allocation models
Data deficits that undermine inter-state trust
Perverse incentives created by minimum support prices and power subsidies
bank.e: Data deficits are classified under operational and political issues. The MSP and power-subsidy point is a policy misalignment across the water–agriculture–energy nexus.

bank.q: Arrange the following tribunal decisions in correct chronological order:
Which institution is proposed to be empowered to build federal consensus on water security?
bank.e: The Inter-State Council, alongside redefining the Centre's Entry 56 role as facilitator rather than only adjudicator.

bank.q: With reference to the Narmada dispute, consider the following statements:
s: Implementation is overseen by the Narmada Control Authority.
bank.e: All three are correct. The Narmada Control Authority is one of the few durable implementation mechanisms to emerge from any Indian water tribunal.
